outcome: For one inbound authorization request, resolve trusted request inputs and complete authorization state inside one authorization evaluation epoch, construct the authorization command only from those resolved facts, and return ALLOW exactly when the existing exact session-role-permission decision admits it; return DENY for every missing, ambiguous, stale, mismatched, incomplete, provider-failed, or epoch-invalid case.
scope: One in-process SQLite-backed Auth Service composition from a correlation-only request_id plus opaque authentication-evidence and route identifiers to one binary authorization decision, with bounded inputs, a single decision time, connection, query-only transaction, trusted-input snapshot, authorization-state snapshot, exact revision joins, and rollback per authorize call.
exclusions: token creation, validation, refresh, or revocation transport
caller-supplied authoritative permission, scope, role, revision, or decision data
implicit schema creation or migration during service startup
audit transport, multi-node operation, deployment, and production-security claims

revision_history.change: Proposed the first complete in-process Auth Service Product Capability and bound ALLOW eligibility to one transaction-scoped authorization evaluation epoch with exact identity, field, and authorization-revision joins.

challenge_route: Challenge service meaning through the Auth Service product owner, snapshot and revision joins through the Auth Foundation definition owner, SQLite epoch correspondence through the Rust implementation owner, and test completeness through the Auth Service product-test owner.
claim_limit: Prototype Product Capability only; it does not adopt product meaning, admit an ontology or DomainSpec source, prove implementation correspondence, approve a product, or authorize activation, publication, release, deployment, or any external effect.
